title: Atomic metering checkpoint for prefetched embeddings and rerank toolchain proration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem summary:
Users report inconsistent billing for non-chat pipelines that do: (1) optimistic/prefetch embedding requests, (2) run a rerank fanout across candidate vectors, and (3) optionally invoke structured output toolcalls. In cases of partial failures, retries, or early cache hits we observe duplicate charge events or missing refunds because the current meter emits charges at multiple points (prefetch, rerank fanout, toolcall) without a single authoritative checkpoint per user request.

Observed failure modes:
- Retry duplication: client retries after transient network failure => prefetched embeddings re-run and charged again because idempotency is not enforced at the billing checkpoint.
- Partial success proration: rerank fanouts where 3/5 candidate calls succeed and 2 fail leave downstream toolcall charges unaccounted or double-billed when fallback executes.
- Cache-then-run: prefix/KV cache hit returns embeddings but the prefetch charge already emitted and not reconciled, causing user-visible overcharge.
- Quota drift: concurrent requests that race quota tokens cause effective oversubscription because metering occurs post-facto.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Introduce an atomic metering checkpoint per top-level non-chat request that is authoritative for billing decisions for all downstream operations (prefetch, rerank, toolcall). This checkpoint is created synchronously at request acceptance with an immutable request_billing_id.
2) Emit "reservation" tokens when work is scheduled; do not finalize charge until checkpoint finalization. Reservations are refundable and have deterministic TTLs.
3) At request completion or terminal failure, run a single reconcile step that: finalizes charges for succeeded units, prorates charges for partially successful fanouts, and issues refunds for cancelled/reserved-but-unused operations.
4) Enforce idempotency by hashing request_billing_id + client_id; duplicate requests with same id are reconciled to a single final charge.
5) Hook billing reconciliation into quota accounting so quota consumption is taken at reservation time and reconciled on finalization to avoid quota drift.

Design considerations / tradeoffs:
- Latency: synchronous checkpoint creation adds a small transaction to request acceptance; we must keep the path <5ms. Use a lightweight in-memory reservation cache with write-behind to the ledger.
- Complexity: introduces new reservation state that needs cleanup; mitigate with deterministic TTL and periodic scavenger process.
- Cost exposure window: customers will see reserved quota; ensure UX in Console indicates "reserved" vs "billed".

Acceptance criteria (must pass for rollout):
- End-to-end integration test covering: cache-hit after prefetch, retry dedupe, partial success rerank proration, toolcall fallback charge semantics.
- Unit tests for reservation creation/finalization/refund logic.
- No regressions in token-level per-request latency beyond +5ms P50.
- Dashboard telemetry showing reservation -> finalization ratio and successful reconciliation for 99.9% of requests in staging.
- Migration plan and compatibility tests for existing customers; default behavior behind feature flag for 2 weeks before full rollout.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Add request_billing_id generation and propagation through the serving runtime and orchestration layer.
- Implement reservation store (in-memory LRU with durable write-behind) and TTL scavenger.
- Modify metering pipeline to accept reservations and defer final charges until reconcile step.
- Extend quota service to consume reservations and reconcile on finalize.
- Update billing ledger APIs to accept idempotent finalize calls that are no-ops if already reconciled.
- Instrument Console to show reserved vs billed counts and to display reconciliation failures.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag behind account-level opt-in. 2) Canary on internal beta tenants (5 orgs) for 48h. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of traffic over 3 days while monitoring refunds and reservation leak metrics. 4) Full rollout after 2 weeks or earlier if metrics stable.

Fallbacks and mitigation:
- If reservation store becomes unhealthy, fallback to current immediate-charge behavior and open an alert.
- Provide automatic refund job to reconcile outstanding reservations older than 72h.
